paper.title: The SEED Encryption Algorithm (RFC 4269; the cipher is the KISA/TTA standard TTAS.KO-12.0004, 1998)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the paper or specification; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: SEED (16-round Feistel, function G from the S-boxes S0/S1 and four masks, three-layer F, key schedule with KC1..KC16) written from RFC 4269 reproduces all four Appendix B test vectors: for each, all 16 pairs of round subkeys (Ki0, Ki1), all 16 states (L0, L1, R0, R1) at the start of each round, and the ciphertext (384 intermediate 32-bit words plus 4 ciphertexts)
The four extended SS-boxes of Appendix A.2 (1,024 entries) equal what the S0/S1 definition and masks give

expected_values_source.what: RFC 4269 Appendix A (S0, S1, SS0-SS3), section 2.3 (KC table) and Appendix B (test vectors with intermediate values)
expected_values_source.note: tables and vectors were copied as data by script from the fetched text; the program was written from the RFC's description. The Korean TTA standard itself was not fetched

negative_control: built with -DSEED_M0=0xFD (mask m0 of function G changed from 0xFC), 512 of the 1,024 SS-box entries differ, 0 of 4 vectors match and the program exits 1
not_checked: the cipher's security claims (the RFC only says no problem has been found) and the CRYPTREC evaluation
decryption (the RFC defines it as reversed subkey order; it is not exercised), other keys than the four, and modes or the OIDs of section 2.5
speed (emulator run time says nothing about any hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the subkeys, round states and ciphertexts RFC 4269 publishes for its four test vectors. It does not show the security claims hold.
